# 1 INFORMATION SYSTEM NAME/TITLE
This System Security Plan provides an overview of the security requirements for the FastTrack Government Cloud (VGC) and describes the controls in place or planned for implementation to provide a level of security appropriate for the information to be transmitted, processed or stored by the system. Information security is vital to our critical infrastructure and its effective performance and protection is a key component of our national security program. Proper management of information technology systems is essential to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data transmitted, processed or stored by the VGC information system.

The security safeguards implemented for the VGC system meet the policy and control requirements set forth in this System Security Plan. All systems are subject to monitoring consistent with applicable laws, regulations, agency policies, procedures and practices.

## 2.1 INFORMATION TYPES

This section describes how the information types used by the information system are categorized for confidentiality, integrity and availability sensitivity levels.

The following tables identify the information types that are input, stored, processed and/or output from VGC. The selection of the information types is based on guidance provided by Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Federal Enterprise Architecture Program Management Office Business Reference Model 2.0 and FIPS Pub 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems which is based on NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-60, Guide for Mapping Types of Information and Information Systems to Security Categories.

The tables also identify the security impact levels for confidentiality, integrity and availability for each of the information types expressed as low, moderate, or high. The security impact levels are based on the potential impact definitions for each of the security objectives (i.e., confidentiality, integrity and availability) discussed in NIST SP 800-60 and FIPS Pub 199.

The potential impact is low if—
- The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability could be expected to have a limited adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.
- A limited adverse effect means that, for example, the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability might: (i) cause a degradation in mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is able to perform its primary functions, but the effectiveness of the functions is noticeably reduced; (ii) result in minor damage to organizational assets; (iii) result in minor financial loss; or (iv) result in minor harm to individuals.

The potential impact is moderate if—
- The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability could be expected to have a serious adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.
- A serious adverse effect means that, for example, the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability might: (i) cause a significant degradation in mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is able to perform its primary functions, but the effectiveness of the functions is significantly reduced; (ii) result in significant damage to organizational assets; (iii) result in significant financial loss; or (iv) result in significant harm to individuals that does not involve loss of life or serious life threatening injuries.

The potential impact is high if—
- The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability could be expected to have a severe or catastrophic adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.
- A severe or catastrophic adverse effect means that, for example, the loss of confidentiality,

integrity, or availability might: (i) cause a severe degradation in or loss of mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is not able to perform one or more of its primary functions; (ii) result in major damage to organizational assets; (iii) result in major financial loss; or (iv) result in severe or catastrophic harm to individuals involving loss of life or serious life threatening injuries.

# 8 INFORMATION SYSTEM TYPE
The VGC makes use of unique managed service provider architecture layer(s).

## 8.1 CLOUD SERVICE MODELS
Information systems, particularly those based on cloud architecture models, are made up of different service layers. Below are some questions that help the system owner determine if their system is a cloud followed by specific questions to help the system owner determine the type of cloud.

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
        <th>Question (Yes/No)</th>
        <th>Conclusion</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td>Does the system use virtual machines?<br/>**Yes**</td>
        <td>A no response means that system is most likely not a cloud.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Does the system have the ability to expand its capacity to meet customer demand?<br/>**Yes**</td>
        <td>A no response means that the system is most likely not a cloud.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Does the system allow the consumer to build anything other than servers?<br/>**Yes**</td>
        <td>A no response means that the system is an IaaS. A yes response means that the system is either a PaaS or an SaaS.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<table>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td>Does the system offer the ability to create databases?<br/>**Yes**</td>
        <td>A yes response means that the system is a PaaS.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Does the system offer various developer toolkits and APIs?<br/>**No**</td>
        <td>A yes response means that the system is a PaaS.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Does the system offer only applications that are available by obtaining a login?<br/>**No**</td>
        <td>A yes response means that system is an SaaS. A no response means that the system is either a PaaS or an IaaS.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<table>
  <thead>

# 9 GENERAL SYSTEM DESCRIPTION

The FastTrack Government Cloud (VGC) is a Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) that allows customers who supports U.S. government organizations the flexibility to customize a scalable public cloud combined with private cloud characteristics. The VGC scales by offering individual Customer Cloud Platform Modules (CCPMs) that are consistent, dedicated virtual devices within a shared infrastructure. Each CCPM contains dedicated physical firewall(s), physical host servers, security and management tool collectors, and a scalable virtual infrastructure. CCPMs are protected by a common security layer, the FastTrack Management Zone (VMZ). Each CCPM is built to the same specifications described in this *VGC System Security Plan Version 9.0, July 26, 2018*. Because each CCPM separated from each other within the VGC boundary, VGC customers have the option of layering on additional security controls based on their unique requirements.

The standard set of tools and services provided to customers by VGC include: firewall management, host and network intrusion detection and prevention services (IDS/IPS), antimalware and malicious code prevention, file integrity monitoring, continuous passive vulnerability scanning, on-demand and automated vulnerability scanning, security information and event management (SIEM), Windows and Red Hat operating system administration, disaster

recovery management, network-through-application monitoring, backup with offsite storage, token-based two-factor authentication, and Remote Desktop Server (the Jumphost), which serves as the sole access point into all hardware, software, networking, and virtual components of VGC.

VGC is hosted at the Cyxtera primary data center DC-5 in Sterling, VA and Equinix primary data center DC10 in Ashburn, VA. Cyxtera and Equinix provide colocation services for FastTrack to host VGC; however, FastTrack owns all of the controls and is responsible for ensuring that all physical and environmental controls are implemented within the VGC physical boundary. The Disaster Recovery (DR) sites for VGC are located at the Cyxtera DN1 data center in Highland Ranch, CO and Equinix SV1 data center in San Jose, CA.

The FastTrack Government Cloud (VGC) was formerly referred to as the FastTrack Government Solutions (FTGS) Federal Community Cloud Platform (FCCP).

## 9.1 SYSTEM FUNCTION OR PURPOSE

The purpose of the VGC is to provide each VGC customer with platform services to help manage virtualized, Microsoft Windows and/or Red Hat Linux operating system virtual servers within a Customer Cloud Platform Module (CCPM) dedicated to that customer. VGC customers include federal agencies, state and local governments, independent software vendors and system integrators. VGC customers install applications, databases and middleware software on the VGC’s operating system platform to support their end customers’ business requirements.

VGC offers the following services to its customers:

*   <u>Data Center</u>: Data center physical environment, including physical security, control access, fire prevention and suppression, air conditioning and humidity control, electricity and Internet connectivity
*   <u>Physical Hardware</u>: Host server, storage and network hardware management, including all required hardware, installation and 24x7 repairs.
*   <u>Virtualization</u>: VMWare hypervisor management, including rapid virtual server provisioning and removal, and preconfigured deployment templates using VMWare vCenter
*   <u>Networking</u>: Router, firewall and switch administration and 24x7 support
*   <u>Security</u>: Network and host-based intrusion detection, log aggregation and inspection, malware and virus protection, vulnerability scanning and remediation, 24x7 incident response
*   <u>Operating System</u>: Platform services to help manage Microsoft Windows and/or Red Hat Linux operating system administration, including monitoring and 24x7 issue response
*   <u>Backup and Disaster recovery</u>: System backups and replication to warm stand by site.

VGC provides computer resources that are ordered by the amount of CPU, memory, and storage capacities documented in the Statement of Work. Computer resources can easily be added or removed when needed.

In order to access a CCPM, each VGC customer must have the Cisco AnyConnect VPN client

installed on the computer that will be used for remote access to the CPM. VGC configures the Cisco AnyConnect VPN client for manual client connection initiation, rather than Cisco Always-on VPN. Additionally, the Cisco AnyConnect VPN client is not licensed for mobile connectivity. VGC has installed the full Cisco AnyConnect VPN client implementing the Essential license. Cisco Anyconnect VPN client uses TLS Version 1.2 FIPS 140-2 encryption to secure the tunnel between the Cisco AnyConnect VPN client and the Cisco ASA endpoint. The Cisco AnyConnect VPN client is configured to require auto-update and to require RSA two-factor authentication. Further, Cisco Anyconnect VPN client is configured to not allow split-tunneling. In addition to requiring Cisco AnyConnect VPN client and RSA two-factor authentication, each VGC Customer must have a valid Active Directory username and password in order to successfully access the Remote Desktop Server (Jumphost). From the Jumphost, VGC customers can access virtual servers in their CCPM as permitted by Active Directory group policies. Further access to the VGC customer application and database within its CCPM can be established as documented and approved in the VGC customer’s System Security Plan.

### Figure 9-2 Authorization Boundary Diagram

Security zones within the VGC authorization boundary include:

A) FastTrack Management Zone (VMZ): host servers - including hypervisor software, storage, network devices, virtual server operating systems and management/security tool software

B) Customer Cloud Platform Module (CCPM) infrastructure: host servers - including hypervisor software, storage, and network devices

C) Management Environment: virtual server operating systems and management/security tool software

**Note:** Customer Environment (D) is not included in the VGC security boundary: virtual server operating systems, application databases, application middleware and application software.

The VGC Authorization Boundary is connected to the Internet using multiple 10 GB cross-connections that are attached to two layer 3 switches that are connected to L3 and Zayo network services. The layer 3 switches are configured in an active-standby state for seamless failover. In the event Layer 3 Switch 1 goes down, Layer 3 Switch 2 can take over the routing of traffic. This provides at least two Internet connection points.

All Customer Cloud Platform Modules (CCPMs) and the FastTrack Management Zone (VMZ) are connected to the VGC Front Switch Stack. Site-to-site VPN’s are configured between the VMZ firewall and the CCPM firewalls. Firewalls are configured as a high availability (HA) pair for redundancy.

The VMZ Switches provide dedicated ports for storage and network connectivity. VMZ ESXi hosts, ports 1 and 2 are assigned for network-related traffic (ex. Vmotion, management, VLAN traffic). Ports 3 and 4 are assigned for VMZ SAN storage related traffic.

To gain access to the FastTrack Management Zone, only VGC System Administrators, VGC Security Engineers, and VGC Network Administrators are assigned a hard RSA token, a user ID, and PIN and passcode to enter this zone. This zone is used only by VGC personnel to manage

The FastTrack Management Zone is connected to VA.SMZ.SW1A and VA.SMZ.SW1B. Within the FastTrack Management Zone are physical hosts: FTGSSMZESXDC501 through FTGSSMZESXDC507, on which the following management virtual servers reside:

*   **BigFix Patch Management:** BigFix Master (mz-bes-01), BigFix Relay, TACACS (mz-tools-01), IBM BigFix Console (mz-bfc-01), BigFix Relay, TACACS (mz-tools-02)
*   **Access Management:** Domain Controller 1 (mz-dc-01), Domain Controller 2 (mz-dc-02), RSA SecurID (mz-rsa-01), TACACS Server (mz-TACACS-01), RDS Jumphost (mz-rds-01)
*   **System and Network Monitoring:** EM7 Web (mz-em7ap-01), EM7 Collector (mz-em7dc-01), EM7 Collector (mz-em7dc-02), EM7 Database (mz-em7db-01), MZ SMTP

(mz-smtp-01)
*   Cloud Orchestration: VMware management: VMWare vCenter (mz-vcn-01), Microsoft SQL Server (mz-sql-01), Microsoft Licensing (mz-kms-01), SMZ Deployment (mz-mdt-01)
*   Security Tools and Scanning: Nessus PSC (mz-psc-01), Nessus and Tools (mz-sectools-01), Trend Micro Deep Sec (mz-trnd-01), Tripwire Console (mz-twc-01), Tripwire Database (mz-twdb-01), Nessus Security Center (mz-nsc-01), FirePOWER IDS (mz-ids-01)
*   Storage and Replication Management: Veeam Replication (mz-veeam-01)
*   System Information Event Management: Splunk (mz-splnk-01), Splunk Forwarder (mz-splunkf-01), Splunk Search Head (splunk-searchhead)

The VMZ includes a storage device that is dedicated to the VMZ. Each CCPM includes a storage device that is dedicated to that CCPM.

> Add architecture digram here

Figure 9-3 VGC Boundary Controls

The following controls protect the VGC security boundaries:
1) The VMZ Firewall controls access between the VMZ (A) and the general Internet.
2) The CCPM Firewall controls access between the CCPM Management Environment (C) and the general Internet
3) The CCPM firewall VLAN controls access between the CCPM Management Environment (C) and the CCPM Customer Environment (D)
4) CCPM-VMZ VPN controls access between the CCPM (B,C,D) and the VMZ (A)
5) VMware isolation and separate storage volumes separate the CCPM Management Environment (C) from the CCPM Customer Environment (D)
6) Physical hardware firewalls, switches and host servers separate one CCPM (B,C,D) from another CCPM (B,C,D).

Access to all VGC authorization boundary zones A, B, C and D. is restricted. Users access the TLS Version 1.2 VPN (FIPS 140-2) using a Cisco AnyConnect client. Successful VPN connectivity requires a User ID, a unique pin, and a passcode, which is randomly generated from an RSA hard token. Finally, to gain access to servers and network resources within the CCPM, users must login with a username and password to a "Jumphost" (Remote Desktop Server).

Each CCPM is self-contained with its own firewalls, switches, and a dedicated management zone that has a Jumphost, RSA Authentication Server, Servers, and Security tools. CCPM firewalls' internal interfaces are configured to hide the internal, private IP addresses that are assigned to hosts and network resources within the CCPM. CCPM firewalls' external interfaces are configured to communicate with the FastTrack Management Zone firewalls located outside of the CCPM boundary and shown in Figure 9-2 Authorization Boundary Diagram. This provides

secure site-to-site VPN communication between the CCPM and the VGC Management Zone, while still allowing outbound connectivity from the CCPM to the public Internet.

VGC Network Administrators configure VLANs to ensure segregated traffic, bound for a particular platform module, does not get misrouted to another tenant’s CCPM; for example, an intentional attack, such as a VLAN Hopping Attack, occurs when Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) is enabled as part of the switch’s configuration. VGC’s Network Administrator disables DTP on all switches within the CPM boundary by setting trunking negotiation to “nonnegotiate,” and prevents attackers from initiating VLAN Hopping attacks.

Each CCPM Management Zone, which is a completely separate entity from the FastTrack Management Zone (VMZ), consists of a security server, a Splunk log collection server, two management host servers, and backup storage server.

On the security server, the following applications reside: ScienceLogic EM7, Cisco FirePOWER, TACACS, Centrify, and Trend Micro Host Intrusion Detection System (HIDS).

On the first management host server, the following reside: Domain Controller, RSA Authentication, RDS Jumphost, BigFix, VMWare management tools, RSA Server, and VMWare vCloud Usage Meter. The second management host server contains one virtual server for VEEAM site to site virtual server replication.

The backup storage server contains Veeam and a secondary domain controller virtual server.

Only the following users have access to the CCPM: VGC System Administrators, VGC Security Engineers, VGC Network Administrators, VGC Domain Administrators, VGC Virtualization Administrators, and VGC CCPM Customer Administrators. To access the CCPM Management Zone and CCPM Customer Zone users are assigned a hard RSA token, a user ID, and PIN and passcode.

Each CCPM has a virtual distributed switch (vSwitch) that separates the Management Environment Zone from the Customer Environment Zone into separate port groups. Port groups define logical boundaries between zones, therefore adding another layer of isolation/segregation. Each CCPM implements port groups only for Production and Development zones. The port groups are restricted to the same layer-2 domain.

Network Interface Card (NIC) teaming is configured on the virtualization platform to provide fault-tolerance/redundancy and additional shared bandwidth. Port channels, which are similar to bonded NICs, are configured on the CCPM firewalls to provide isolation between tenants using VLAN segmentation.

Each CCPM has its own TLS Version 1.2 VPN (FIPS 140-2) tunnel secured by SSL for its users to authenticate and access the environment. Users from one CPM are not be able to access a different CPM.

There are currently 80 internal personnel and 0 external personnel. Within one year, it is anticipated that there will be 90 internal personnel and 0 external personnel.

The following account types have been defined: Security Engineer, Network Administrator, System Administrator, Domain Administrator, Virtualization Administrator, Security Analyst, and Program Manager. Individuals assigned as Security Engineers may not be assigned to any other account type.

The VGC Domain Administrator establishes the following groups:

* Security Engineer Group
* Network Administrator Group
* System Administrator Group
* Appliance Administrator Group
* Domain Administrator Group
* Virtualization Administrator Group
* Customer Administrator Group

To approve and set up an employee newly assigned to support a Cloud Module: The Program Manager assigns new employees one or more VGC roles and account types. The Security Analyst provides new employees with 1) Remote Access Approval form, 2) Security Awareness Training, and 3) Background check forms required by VGC Program Manager. Each CCPM Customer System Owner signs Remote Access Approval form, indicating that new employee is granted system access with Account Type access permissions. The Domain Administrator assigns an account and provides new employees with access credentials and permissions based on account type. There are no group accounts.

To identify authorized users, once they are approved by the CCPM Customer System Owner, the Domain Administrator assigns a unique user name to employees and configures Active Directory (AD) with appropriate privileges as defined by RBAC. The Domain Administrator configures the RSA system and distributes an RSA token to new employees. The user is required to establish a four-digit pin number to be used in conjunction with the randomly generated passcode from the RSA token to establish a VPN connection. Once the VPN connection is established, the user can connect to an RDP session to access the Jumphost. Upon first login, the user enters the temporary AD password, which they are then prompted to change. The Security Engineer, Network Administrator, System Administrator, and Domain Administrator access the systems using the assigned User Name and RSA PIN along with the temporary passcode generated by the RSA token. All account types must initially access a Remote Desktop Services "Jumphost."

The Jumphost serves as the sole access point into all hardware, software, networking, and virtual components of the VGC and are managed by VGC. To access the Jumphost, the user inputs their User Name and AD Password. The Security Engineer, Network Administrator, System Administrator, and Domain Administrator may only access devices and software as defined by RBAC for assigned account types from the Remote Desktop Services "Jumphost."

After the CCPM Customer System Owner receives notification that the employee is cleared to work, the CCPM Customer System Owner, CCPM Customer System Owner, and the VGC Program Manager sign the Remote Access Approval Form. The Security Analyst retains the documents in OneDrive and notifies the Domain Administrator to create the account and assign appropriate privileges. Domain Administrators establish the account, based on role, in "Active Directory Users and Computers" Microsoft Management Console (MMC). The user is given a unique ID and temporary password, which needs to be changed at first logon. Linux: Once the government approves account requests, either local or domain accounts are setup based on role RBAC. VGC System Administrators install and configure WinBIND to link AD accounts to Linux Machine Accounts.

To activate the local accounts, the account is configured to 'enabled'. For domain accounts, the setting is changed from 'disabled' to 'enabled'. System administrators can modify and disable accounts by changing settings in AD for domain accounts and local accounts. For local and domain accounts, accounts are removed from the AD domain or from local account lists. Windows: Domain Administrators create and enable the account, based on role, in AD Users and Computers MMC. The user is given a unique ID and temporary password, which needs to be changed at first logon. To activate the account, the Domain Administrator unchecks the 'Account is Disabled' checkbox within the 'Account Options' of the AD MMC. To modify the account, only privileged users can access the 'User Properties' section of the AD MMC to make changes. To disable an account, the Domain Administrator checks the 'Account is Disabled' checkbox within the 'Account Options' of the AD MMC. To remove an account, the Domain Administrator goes to 'User Account Properties' within AD MMC and clicks 'Delete Account'. For non-user accounts, as soon as VGC receives a notification, either via email or telephone, from the VGC Customer that the accounts are no longer needed, they are disabled immediately and removed within 60 days.

The CCPM Customer System Owner has sole authority to request the following actions be performed by submitting a change request to VGC Operations team via ServiceNOW ticketing system:

* Add or remove CPM virtual servers to the CCPM Production or Staging/Test Zones.
* Add or remove compute resources (CPU, memory, disk) to any CPM virtual server located in the CPM Production or Staging/Test Zones.
* Change allocations of compute resources to CCPM virtual servers located in the CPM Production or Staging/Test zones.
* Authorize access or removal of access of CCPM Customer Administrators for user access to virtual server operating systems located in the CPM Production or Staging/Test zones via the Customer Administrator Group.
* Authorize access or removal of access of the CCPM Customer Administrator Group for specific database or application processes located in the CPM Production or Staging/Test zones as specified in Customer SSP.
* Authorize cutover of CCPM Production or Staging/Test zone service to the VGC Disaster Recovery site per the VGC Contingency Plan.
* Authorize Configuration changes to the network infrastructure in support of the database and application
* Establish patch schedule and reporting requirements for their Customer Environment.

The CCPM Customer Administrator is responsible for installing and administering database and applications in the CCPM Production or Staging/Test zone per security controls described in the Customer SSP. The CCPM Customer Administrator can notify FTGS of any performance, availability issues in the VGC CCPM environment or any support requests via a ServiceNow trouble ticket.

Figure 9-2 Authorization Boundary Diagram, provides an architecture diagram of the VGC hosting multiple CCPMs.

VGC disaster recovery sites are located at Cyxtera DN1 data center in Highland Ranch, CO and Equinix SV1 data center in San Jose, CA. The disaster recovery sites contain the same physical security measures as the Cyxtera primary DC5 data center in Sterling, VA, and Equinix primary data center in Ashburn, VA.

Traffic from the Internet passes through Layer 3 Switch Stack to the DR MZ Firewall and DR CCPM Firewall allows traffic to pass through to the hosts where the individual DR CCPMs reside and to the DR VGC Management Zone. There are site-to-site VPN connections between the DR MZ Firewall and the DR CCPM Firewalls.

Within the DR-FastTrack Management Zone are physical hosts: The first is DR-VGC-MGMTHOST, on which virtual servers reside:

1. Domain Controller (DR-VGC-DC01)
2. Nessus Server (DR-VGC-SCAN01)
3. Remote Desktop Server [(RDS/Jumphost) DR-VGC-RDS01]
4. RSA Authentication Server (DR-VGC-RSAVApp01)
5. Encryption Key Management Server (DR-VGC-ENCRYP01)

The second host server is DR-VGC-MGMTHOST02, which contains one virtual server for data replication (DR-VGC-VEEAM01)

In addition, a Backup Storage Management Server (DR-VGC-BACKUP01) houses a second domain controller (DR-VGC-DC02) and resides in the management zone.

Finally, the shared storage (DR-VGC-STG01) is provisioned to each individual cloud platform modules via their hosts.

*VGC Disaster Recovery Site*

The following architectural diagram(s), provides a visual depiction of the individual VGC DR CCPM Disaster Recovery Site in Highland Ranch, CO. Note that the DR CCPM is not operational and its function is to provide the template configurations for all DR CCPM’s that are running in VGC. See ATTACHMENT 13 – FedRAMP Inventory Workbook for each DR CCPM Architecture.

The figure "VGC CCPM Architecture," in section 9.4, shows the DR-CCPM is equipped with its own dedicated firewall, DR-CCPM-FW01 and a dedicated switch DR-CCPM-SW01, providing a second layer of security. The DR-CCPM firewalls are configured to deny all inbound traffic. 'Explicit Allow' access control lists (ACLs) are configured based on customer request and are addressed through VGC's change control process.

Once inside the CPM, access to all zones is restricted. In addition to the multiple layers of security that firewalls and VLANs provide, CPMs are further secured by segmenting them into the following zones: CCPM management zone, CCPM production zone, and CCPM staging/test zone.

The DR-CCPM Management Zone, which is a completely separate entity from the DR-VGC Management Zone, consists of a security server, a management host server, and a backup server. On the security server, the following applications reside: EM7, FirePOWER, TACACS, Centrify, and Trend Micro Host Intrusion Detection System (HIDS). On the management host server, the following reside: Domain Controller, RSA Authentication, RDS Jumphost, BigFix, Storage Manager, and VMWare VCenter, RSA Server, and vCloud Usage Meter. On the backup server, the following resides: Veeam, virtual tape library, and a secondary domain controller.

The CCPM Production Zone consists of the VGC Customer's Web server, application server, and database server. The CCPM Staging/Test Zone is testing ground with a subset of the components in the production zone.

## 10.1 DATA FLOW

Users access the VPN using a Cisco AnyConnect Client. Successful VPN connectivity requires a User ID, a unique pin, and a passcode, which is randomly generated from an RSA hard token. For administrative traffic (i.e., VGC System Administrators, VGC Network Administrators, VGC Security Engineers, VGC Domain Administrators) coming in to the VGC environment, Port 3389 (RDP) inbound is open on the MZ Firewalls or to the specific CCPM Firewalls.

For VGC Customer traffic, port 3389 on each CCPM firewalls is open to allow incoming traffic. Each CCPM firewalls are set up with Network Address Translation (NAT), ensuring connectivity to the shared firewall while securing each internal CCPM environment. This is achieved through the use of private, non-routable IP addresses. A private IP address on each CCPM firewall is NAT’d to the public address on the shared firewall.

Once inside the CCPM, access to all zones is restricted because each zone is on a different subnet. Finally, to gain access to servers and network resources within the CCPM, users must login with a username and password to a Remote Desktop Server “Jumphost” (For CCPM: CCPM-RDS01). The following ports are open: For IPsec, UDP500, and UDP 4500; for VPN Client, TCP 10000; and for TLS Version 1.2, TCP 465.

All other types of customer data flow required by the customer’s database, applications or middleware software, must be document and approved in the VGC customer’s System Security Plan. If any of these data flows require configuration changes to the firewall, a Change Request form must be completed and approved by the VGC Change Control Board (CCB). For example, a customer requesting traffic to and from the database, would request TCP port 1433 to be opened on the CPM firewalls (for CCPM: RPCM-FW01 and RPCM-FW2) and documented in the VGC customer SSP.

# 13 MINIMUM SECURITY CONTROLS

Security controls must meet minimum security control baseline requirements. Upon categorizing a system as Low, Moderate, or High sensitivity in accordance with FIPS 199, the corresponding security control baseline standards apply. Some of the control baselines have enhanced controls which are indicated in parentheses.

Security controls that are representative of the sensitivity of VGC are described in the sections that follow. Security controls that are designated as "Not Selected" or "Withdrawn by NIST" are not described unless they have additional FedRAMP controls. Guidance on how to describe the implemented standard can be found in NIST 800-53, Rev 4. Control enhancements are marked in parentheses in the sensitivity columns.

Systems that are categorized as FIPS 199 Low use the controls designated as Low, systems categorized as FIPS 199 Moderate use the controls designated as Moderate and systems categorized as FIPS 199 High use the controls designated as High. A summary of which security standards pertain to which sensitivity level is found in Table 13-1 Summary of Required Security Controls that follows.

## 13.1 ACCESS CONTROL (AC)

### AC-1 Access Control Policy and Procedures Requirements (L) (M)

The organization:

(a) Develops, documents and disseminates to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]:
(1) An access control policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and
(2) Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the access control policy and associated access controls; and

(b) Reviews and updates the current:
(1) Access control policy [FedRAMP Assignment: at least every 3 years]; and
(2) Access control procedures [FedRAMP Assignment: at least annually].

# AC-2 Account Management (L) (M)

The organization:
(a) Identifies and selects the following types of information system accounts to support organizational missions/business functions: [*Assignment: organization-defined information system account types*];
(a) Assigns account managers for information system accounts;
(b) Establishes conditions for group and role membership;
(c) Specifies authorized users of the information system, group and role membership, and access authorizations (i.e., privileges) and other attributes (as required) for each account;
(d) Requires approvals by [*Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles*] for requests to create information system accounts;
(e) Creates, enables, modifies, disables, and removes information system accounts in accordance with [*Assignment: organization-defined procedures or conditions*];
(f) Monitors the use of information system accounts;
(g) Notifies account managers:
(1) When accounts are no longer required;
(2) When users are terminated or transferred; and
(3) When individual information system usage or need-to-know changes;
(h) Authorizes access to the information system based on:
(1) A valid access authorization;
(2) Intended system usage; and
(3) Other attributes as required by the organization or associated missions/business functions;
(i) Reviews accounts for compliance with account management requirements [*FedRAMP Assignment: at least annually*]; and
(j) Establishes a process for reissuing shared/group account credentials (if deployed) when individuals are removed from the group.

The VGC System Administrator establishes local accounts for Network Administrators for network appliances, (firewalls, load balancers, switches) based on role (RBAC). VGC Technical Account Managers and the VGC CPM Customer Administrator issues a work order in ServiceNow to modify a user account and makes the appropriate change. Once the VGC System Administrator creates an account in Linux, it is automatically activated. To disable accounts, the account is configured to 'disable', preventing access. The account is removed upon request via email from the VGC CPM Customer Administrator or CPM Customer System Owner.<br/><br/>**Windows:** Domain Administrators create and enable the account, based on role, in AD Users and MMC. The user is given a unique ID and temporary password, which needs to be changed at first logon. To activate the account, the Domain Administrator unchecks the 'Account is Disabled' checkbox within the 'Account Options' of the AD MMC. To modify the account, only privileged users can access the 'User Properties' section of the AD MMC to make changes. To disable an account, the Domain Administrator checks the 'Account is Disabled' checkbox within the 'Account Options' of the AD MMC. To remove an account, the Domain Administrator goes to 'User Account Properties' within AD MMC and clicks 'Delete Account'. For non-user accounts (such as service accounts and accounts associated with devices), as soon as VGC receives a notification, either via email or telephone, from the VGC Customer that the accounts are no longer needed, they are disabled and removed within 60 days.<br/><br/>**Networking:** Routers, Switches, Firewalls, and Load balancers use a scaled-down version of Linux. Network devices use TACACS for central authentication, authorization, and accountability (AAA). The VGC Network Administrator establishes and activates local accounts based on role within each appliance's account configuration settings. VGC Network Administrator issues a work order in ServiceNow to modify a user account and make the appropriate change, including disabling and removing a user who is no longer authorized to have access.<br/><br/>**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for notifying account managers when temporary accounts are no longer required and when information system users are terminated, transferred, or information system usage or need-to-know/need-to-share changes for application and database accounts. ### AC-3 (4) Control Enhancement (IL4)
The information system enforces *[Assignment: organization-defined discretionary access control policies]* over defined subjects and objects where the policy specifies that a subject that has been granted access to information can do one or more of the following:
(a) Pass the information to any other subjects or objects;
(b) Grant its privileges to other subjects;
(c) Change security attributes on subjects, objects, the information system, or the information system’s components;
(d) Choose the security attributes to be associated with newly created or revised objects; or
(e) Change the rules governing access control.

Supplemental Guidance: When discretionary access control policies are implemented, subjects are not constrained with regard to what actions they can take with information for which they have already been granted access. Thus, subjects that have been granted access to information are not prevented from passing (i.e., the subjects have the discretion to pass) the information to other subjects or objects. This control enhancement can operate in conjunction with AC-3 (3). A subject that is constrained in its operation by policies governed by AC-3 (3) is still able to

operate under the less rigorous constraints of this control enhancement. Thus, while AC-3 (3) imposes constraints preventing a subject from passing information to another subject operating at a different sensitivity level, AC-3 (4) permits the subject to pass the information to any subject at the same sensitivity level. The policy is bounded by the information system boundary. Once the information is passed outside of the control of the information system, additional means may be required to ensure that the constraints remain in effect. While the older, more traditional definitions of discretionary access control require identity-based access control, that limitation is not required for this use of discretionary access control.

## AC-8 System Use Notification (L) (M) (H)
The information system:
(a) Displays to users *[Assignment: organization-defined system use notification message or banner (FedRAMP Assignment: see additional Requirements and Guidance)]* before granting access to the system that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance and states that:
* (1) Users are accessing a U.S. Government information system;
* (2) Information system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit;
* (3) Unauthorized use of the information system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and
* (4) Use of the information system indicates consent to monitoring and recording;

(a) Retains the notification message or banner on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the information system; and

(c) For publicly accessible systems:
> (1) Displays system use information [*Assignment: organization-defined conditions (FedRAMP Assignment: see additional Requirements and Guidance)*], before granting further access;
> (2) Displays references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing that are consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems that generally prohibit those activities; and
> (3) Includes a description of the authorized uses of the system.

**AC-8 Additional FedRAMP Requirements and Guidance:**

**Requirement:** The service provider shall determine elements of the cloud environment that require the System Use Notification control. The elements of the cloud environment that require System Use Notification are approved and accepted by the JAB/AO.

**Requirement:** The service provider shall determine how System Use Notification is going to be verified and provide appropriate periodicity of the check. The System Use Notification verification and periodicity are approved and accepted by the JAB/AO.

**Guidance:** If performed as part of a Configuration Baseline check, then the % of items requiring setting that are checked and that pass (or fail) check can be provided.

**Requirement:** If not performed as part of a Configuration Baseline check, then there must be documented agreement on how to provide results of verification and the necessary periodicity of the verification by the service provider. The documented agreement on how to provide verification of the results are approved and accepted by the JAB/AO.

        <td>**Implemented**<br/>**Shared (Service Provider and Customer Responsibility)**<br/>**VGC:** VGC System Administrators, prior to system build, configure the warning banner that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance and states that: (i) users are accessing a U.S. Government information system; (ii) system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; (iii) unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and (iv) use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.<br/>- For Windows servers the warning banner text appears after successfully logging on via RDP. The warning banner is configured in Active Directory<br/>- For Linux servers the warning banner text appears after successfully logging on via SSH<br/>- For network devices the warning banner text appears after successfully logging on via SSH<br/>- For VMware the warning banner text appears after successfully logging on via the vSphere client<br/>**IL4 Implementation:** Same as VGC implementation. As part of its vendor analysis strategy, VGC performs a thorough evaluation and comparison of all cloud environment components to ensure they meet contractual requirements as stated in the Statement of Work or Work Order. To meet this particular control, FTGS will procure infrastructure hardware and software components that have a customer configurable capability to support a logon banner having a minimum of 1300 characters that is displayed and acknowledged before any logon prompt offered to privileged and non-privileged customer users.<br/>**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for displaying an approved system use notification message or banner before granting access to the application or database that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance and states that: (i) users are accessing a U.S. Government information system; (ii) system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; (iii) unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and (iv) use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Part b</td>
        <td>**Implemented**<br/>**Shared (Service Provider and Customer Responsibility)**<br/>**VGC:** VGC System Administrators configure the banner to remain on the screen indefinitely until the user clicks ‘ok’. For Linux servers, the warning banner is on the same page as the login screen. VGC System Administrators check for new banner language as part of the baseline configuration review/update.<br/>**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for retaining the notification message or banner on the screen until users take explicit actions to log on to or further access the information system.</td>
    </tr>

### Additional FedRAMP Requirements and Guidance

**Requirement 1:** The service provider shall determine elements of the cloud environment that require the System Use Notification control. The elements of the cloud environment that require System Use Notification are approved and accepted by the JAB/AO.

**Requirement 2:** The service provider shall determine how System Use Notification is going to be verified and provide appropriate periodicity of the check. The System Use Notification verification and periodicity are approved and accepted by the JAB/AO. If performed as part of a Configuration Baseline check, then the % of items requiring setting that are checked and that pass (or fail) check can be provided.

**Requirement 3:** If not performed as part of a Configuration Baseline check, then there must be documented agreement on how to provide results of verification and the necessary periodicity of the verification by the service provider. The documented agreement on how to provide verification of the results are approved and accepted by the JAB/AO.

## AC-16 Security Attributes (IL4)
The organization:
> a. Provides the means to associate [Assignment: organization-defined types of security attributes] having [Assignment: organization-defined security attribute values] with

information in storage, in process, and/or in transmission;

b. Ensures that the security attribute associations are made and retained with the information;

c. Establishes the permitted [Assignment: organization-defined security attributes] for [Assignment: organization-defined information systems]; and

d. Determines the permitted [Assignment: organization-defined values or ranges] for each of the established security attributes.

Supplemental Guidance: Information is represented internally within information systems using abstractions known as data structures. Internal data structures can represent different types of entities, both active and passive. Active entities, also known as subjects, are typically associated with individuals, devices, or processes acting on behalf of individuals. Passive entities, also known as objects, are typically associated with data structures such as records, buffers, tables, files, inter-process pipes, and communications ports. Security attributes, a form of metadata, are abstractions representing the basic properties or characteristics of active and passive entities with respect to safeguarding information. These attributes may be associated with active entities (i.e., subjects) that have the potential to send or receive information, to cause information to flow among objects, or to change the information system state. These attributes may also be associated with passive entities (i.e., objects) that contain or receive information. The association of security attributes to subjects and objects is referred to as binding and is typically inclusive of setting the attribute value and the attribute type. Security attributes when bound to data/information, enables the enforcement of information security policies for access control and information flow control, either through organizational processes or information system functions or mechanisms. The content or assigned values of security attributes can directly affect the ability of individuals to access organizational information. Organizations can define the types of attributes needed for selected information systems to support missions/business functions. There is potentially a wide range of values that can be assigned to any given security attribute. Release markings could include, for example, US only, NATO, or NOFORN (not releasable to foreign nationals). By specifying permitted attribute ranges and values, organizations can ensure that the security attribute values are meaningful and relevant. The term security labeling refers to the association of security attributes with subjects and objects represented by internal data structures within organizational information systems, to enable information system-based enforcement of information security policies. Security labels include, for example, access authorizations, data life cycle protection (i.e., encryption and data expiration), nationality, affiliation as contractor, and classification of information in accordance with legal and compliance requirements. The term security marking refers to the association of security attributes with objects in a human-readable form, to enable organizational process-based enforcement of information security policies. The AC-16 base control represents the requirement for user-based attribute association (marking). The enhancements to AC-16 represent additional requirements including information system-based attribute association (labeling). Types of attributes include, for example, classification level for objects and clearance (access authorization) level for subjects. An example of a value for both of these attribute types is Top Secret. Related controls: AC-3, AC-4, AC-6, AC-21, AU-2, AU-10, SC-16, MP-3.

        <td rowspan="2">Implemented<br/><br/>**Shared (Service Provider and Customer Responsibility)**<br/><br/>**VGC:** After receiving approval to access the management zone via the Remote Access Approval form, VGC System Administrators, VGC Domain Administrators, VGC Network Administrators, VGC Virtualization Administrators, and VGC Security Engineers access the Jumphost using a Cisco AnyConnect VPN Client (TCP 10000) using Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP) secured by TLS Version 1.2 encryption at both ends of the VPN tunnel. These privileged users log into the VPN with a user ID, a unique PIN, and a passcode that is randomly generated from an RSA hardware token (UDP 5500). After establishing the VPN connection, VGC System Administrators, VGC Domain Administrators, VGC Network Administrators, VGC Virtualization Administrators, and VGC Security Engineers access all servers and network devices only through a Microsoft Remote Desktop Server, using Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) Port 3389. Only authorized privileged users access the VGC system in the above-described manner.<br/><br/>**Customer Responsibility:** Since the VGC CPM Customer Administrator is an authorized privileged role, the VGC CPM Administrator accesses the management zone using the same process as the VGC System Administrators, VGC Domain Administrators, VGC Network Administrators, VGC Virtualization Administrators, and VGC Security Engineers. The VGC CPM Customer Administrator would need to gain remote access to the VGC system before granting access to its users to the application and database. The VGC CPM Customer is responsible for describing how its users gain remote access in its SSP.</td>
        <td></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Part b</td>
        <td rowspan="2">Implemented<br/><br/>**Service Provider Corporate**<br/><br/>**VGC:** Access is not given to any personnel until the CPM Customer System Owner, the VGC Program Manager, and the Administrator sign the Remote Access Approval Form. After the form is signed, the Domain Administrator creates the specific administrator account, issuing a user ID, temporary password, and RSA token.</td>
    </tr>

The Cisco AnyConnect VPN client authenticates to the Cisco ASA Firewall, which use TLS Version 1.2 FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules. The Remote Desktop Connection uses 128-bit TLS 1.2 encryption and is used to access either “Jumphost” from the Cisco ASA Firewall. To protect integrity, IPsec, TLS Version 1.2, and RSA are used. ## AC-23 Data Mining Protection (IL4)

The organization employs [Assignment: organization-defined data mining prevention and detection techniques] for [Assignment: organization-defined data storage objects] to adequately detect and protect against data mining.

Supplemental Guidance: Data storage objects include, for example, databases, database records, and database fields. Data mining prevention and detection techniques include, for example: (i) limiting the types of responses provided to database queries; (ii) limiting the number/frequency of database queries to increase the work factor needed to determine the contents of such databases; and (iii) notifying organizational personnel when atypical database queries or accesses occur. This control focuses on the protection of organizational information from data mining while such information resides in organizational data stores. In contrast, AU-13 focuses on monitoring for organizational information that may have been mined or otherwise obtained from data stores and is now available as open source information residing on external sites, for example, through social networking or social media websites.

    <tr>
        <td>Part a</td>
        <td>**IL4 Implementation:** For DoD agency customer environments, the ISSO or security representative may choose to adopt similar security training as that of FTGS for recognition of malicious and anomalous activity. As part of its defense in depth strategy FTGS Corporate Security Awareness training includes modules that pertain to recognizing malicious code. Personnel are trained to look for indications of potentially suspicious email (e.g., receiving an unexpected email, receiving an email containing strange or poor grammar, or receiving an email from an unfamiliar sender but who appears to be from a known sponsor or contractor). Personnel are also trained on how to respond to such suspicious email or web communications (e.g., not opening attachments, not clicking on embedded web links, and checking the source of email addresses). For this process to work effectively, all organizational personnel are trained and made aware of what constitutes suspicious communications.) The training has a greater chance of success for helping personnel correctly identify actual malicious and anomalous communications and objects because the training modules are designed to be interactive, requiring personnel to directly select objects on the screen which represent potentially malicious objects and malicious communications, in a controlled environment.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

## AU-2 Audit Events (L) (M) (H)

(a) Coordinates the security audit function with other organizational entities requiring audit-related information to enhance mutual support and to help guide the selection of auditable events;
(b) Provides a rationale for why the auditable events are deemed to be adequate to

support after-the-fact investigations of security incidents; and

(c) Determines that the following events are to be audited within the information system: [*FedRAMP Assignment: organization-defined subset of the auditable events defined in AU-2 a. to be audited continually for each identified event*].

### AU-4 (1) Control Enhancement (IL4)
The information system off-loads audit records [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] onto a different system or media than the system being audited.

Supplemental Guidance: Off-loading is a process designed to preserve the confidentiality and integrity of audit records by moving the records from the primary information system to a

secondary or alternate system. It is a common process in information systems with limited audit storage capacity; the audit storage is used only in a transitory fashion until the system can communicate with the secondary or alternate system designated for storing the audit records, at which point the information is transferred.

Suspicious events are reported via email to the VGC Program Manager to promote situational awareness.<br/><br/>**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for analyzing and correlating audit records across different repositories within the application and database to gain organization-wide situational awareness. In addition, the VGC Customer may request application and database logs that are captured by Splunk from the VGC Security Engineer. ### AU-7 Audit Reduction and Report Generation (M) (H)
The information system provides an audit reduction and report generation capability that:
(a) Supports on-demand audit review, analysis, and reporting requirements and after-the-fact investigations of security incidents; and

(b) Does not alter the original content or time ordering of audit records.

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
        <th>AU-7</th>
        <th>Control Summary Information</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td colspan="2">Responsible Role: VGC Security Engineer, VGC Customer</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td colspan="2">Implementation Status (check all that apply):<br/>[x] Implemented<br/>[ ] Partially implemented<br/>[ ] Planned<br/>[ ] Alternative implementation<br/>[ ] Not applicable</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td colspan="2">Control Origination (check all that apply):<br/>[x] Service Provider Corporate<br/>[ ] Service Provider System Specific<br/>[ ] Service Provider Hybrid (Corporate and System Specific)<br/>[ ] Configured by Customer (Customer System Specific)<br/>[ ] Provided by Customer (Customer System Specific)<br/>[ ] Shared (Service Provider and Customer Responsibility)<br/>[ ] Inherited from pre-existing FedRAMP Authorization for Click here to enter text. , Date of Authorization</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
        <th></th>
        <th colspan="2">AU-7 What is the solution and how is it implemented?</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td>Part a</td>
        <td>**Implemented**<br/>**Service Provider Corporate**<br/>**VGC:** The VGC Security Engineer configures Splunk to provide an audit reduction and report generation capability that supports on-demand audit review, analysis, and reporting requirements and after-the-fact investigations of security incidents. VGC Security Engineer sets up the Splunk Indexer to receive logs from all virtual servers and network devices by installing a splunkforwarders on all nodes within the VGC accreditation boundary. In addition VGC Engineer configures Splunk Heavy Forwarders for each customer CPM. The splunkforwarder sends its logs to the Heavy Forwarder, which parses and forwards it onto the Splunk Indexer. The VGC Security Engineer creates a cron job on the Splunk Indexer to truncate logs after 365 days for audit reduction purposes. Within Splunk, audit logs reside in buckets. Current logs reside in warm buckets. After the one-year retention period, the audit logs are moved to cold buckets. Splunk is configured to perform audit record reduction by moving logs from the warm buckets to cold buckets after the defined retention period.<br/>The VGC Security Engineer sets up reporting on the Splunk Indexer by inputting a search in the Search field of the Splunk GUI using SPL, the Splunk search processing language, running this search, saving this search as a Report, defining the report criteria, and then setting it to run on a regular schedule based on agency customer and FedRAMP requirements. These reports can also be generated for on-demand reviews,analysis, and after-the-fact investigations. In addition the Visualization tab on the Search page of the Splunk GUI provides the capability to perform deep analysis of the data based on the search string.</td>
        <td></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Part b</td>
        <td>**Implemented**<br/>**Service Provider Corporate**<br/>**VGC:** The VGC Security Engineer configures Splunk to pull it's time settings from the primary domain controller in the VGC Shared Management Zone (SMZ) which uses NIST ntp servers as the authoritative time source for all VGC SMZ management tools, servers, and network devices. Having Splunk synchronize to the same time source as all nodes in the VGC accreditation means all audit records are also using the same time source. In addition logs that come in are timestamped based on when they were generated. The original content and time ordering of logs is protected from alteration by TLS encryption between the splunkforwarder, Heavy Forwarder, and Splunk Indexer during transmission and this integrity is maintained as the logs are automatically moved from hot buckets, to warm buckets, to cold buckets as the logs age.</td>
        <td></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

The VGC Network Administrator configures all network appliances to use the domain controller to generate timestamps. Since VGC Security Engineer configures Splunk to get its time settings from the domain controller which in turn uses NIST NTP servers as its authoritative time source, these NTP servers are configured to map to UTC settings and therefore timestamps for all records received by Splunk are mapped to UTC settings, meeting one second granularity of time measurement.<br/><br/>**IL4 Implementation:** Same as VGC implementation.</td>

### AU-8 (1) Control Enhancement (M) (H)
The information system:
> (a) Compares the internal information system clocks with [*FedRAMP Assignment:*

authoritative time source: [http://tf.nist.gov/tf-cgi/servers.cgi] [at least hourly]]; and

(b) Synchronizes the internal system clocks to the authoritative time source when the time difference is greater than [Assignment: organization-defined time period].

**AU-8 (1) Additional FedRAMP Requirements and Guidance:**

**Requirement:** The service provider selects primary and secondary time servers used by the NIST Internet time service. The secondary server is selected from a different geographic region than the primary server.

**Requirement:** The service provider synchronizes the system clocks of network computers that run operating systems other than Windows to the Windows Server Domain Controller emulator or to the same time source for that server.

**Guidance:** The service provider selects primary and secondary time servers used by the NIST Internet time service, or by a Stratum-1 time server. The secondary server is selected from a different geographic region than the primary server.

If using Windows Active Directory, all servers should synchronize time with the time source for the Windows Domain Controller. If using some other directory services (e.g., LDAP), all servers should synchronize time with the time source for the directory server

### CA-7 Continuous Monitoring (L) (M) (H)

The organization develops a continuous monitoring strategy and implements a continuous monitoring program that includes:

(a) Establishment of [Assignment: organization-defined metrics] to be monitored;
(b) Establishment of [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for monitoring and [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for assessments supporting such monitoring;
(c) Ongoing security control assessments in accordance with the organizational

continuous monitoring strategy;

(d) Ongoing security status monitoring of organization-defined metrics in accordance with the organizational continuous monitoring strategy;

(e) Correlation and analysis of security-related information generated by assessments and monitoring;

(f) Response actions to address results of the analysis of security-related information; and

(g) Reporting the security status of organization and the information system to [*FedRAMP Assignment: to meet Federal and FedRAMP requirements*] [*Assignment: organization-defined frequency*].

> **Guidance:** CSPs must provide evidence of closure and remediation of a high vulnerability within the timeframe for standard POA&M updates.

Based on the specific requirements, the following components are configured by the appropriate administrator/engineer:<br/><br/>● The VGC Virtualization Administrator installs and configures the VMware ESXi hypervisor to prepare it for the operating system installation. The ESXi hypervisor resides on physical management hosts which are connected to the VGC switches.<br/>● The VGC System Administrator installs and configures Windows and Linux operating systems onto the virtual servers which reside on the physical management hosts.<br/>● The VGC Network Administrator configures switches to segregate traffic via separate physical ports which connect separate physical devices.<br/>● The VGC Network Administrator configures firewalls in a high availability (HA) pair to provide redundancy. The primary and secondary firewalls are configured as active and passive respectively.<br/>● The VGC Security Engineer configures the environment with a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) to detect anomalous traffic. The NIDS is connected to two switch ports: one switch port for management and the second switch port for port mirroring (sniffing traffic).<br/>● The VGC System Administrator configures storage devices to provide shared storage to virtual servers within the VGC accreditation boundary. Shared storage is connected to the VGC switch. There are two management paths for shared storage to provide redundancy.     <tr>
        <td>by assessing the configurations against defined benchmark settings and documenting any deviations from the defined benchmark. This baseline information is stored in VGC’s OneDrive system and are available upon request to the 3PAO.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;In addition, the following tools automatically develop baselines when initially installed and configured and maintain baselines by comparing any changes to the baseline as the system is being used:&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;BigFix, which centrally manages deployment of patches, updates, and hotfixes initially takes a baseline of patch levels, versions, and other attributes of all nodes that report to it. As these nodes baseline changes from use and as new patches, hotfixes, and updates become available BigFix is automatically updated to reflect the deviations from the baseline through client relays, installed on each node and top-level relays installed in the SMZ.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Trend Micro, an antivirus and host intrusion detection system, also automatically develops and maintains a baseline of the virtual servers and network devices that report to it when it is initially installed. Trend Micro receives updates of any changes to the baseline configuration of each node that reports to it via installed agents. FTGS Security Engineer create policies on Trend Micro to automatically alert via email of any configuration changes, file changes, registry changes, etc. that meet a predefined threshold to deem the change a risk to the system’s integrity.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Trend Micro Deep Security automatically develops and maintains a baseline configuration by design since the antimalware, intrusion detection/prevention, log inspection, and firewall capabilities all use a heuristic/pattern analysis engine to compare any changes to the servers and network devices that report to it against the original baseline.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Tenable Security Center, which centrally manages vulnerability scanning for all servers and network devices in the VGC accreditation boundary, develops and maintains baselines of the OS, firmware, versions, ports, protocols, and services that are installed on each component that is scanned. Any changes to the original baseline is stored in the back-end database that Security Center uses to store scans and reports. The reporting feature provides a historical record of all changes to the baseline, which is useful for troubleshooting failed scans, performing forensic analysis, and overall vulnerability management.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;Tripwire provides the following file integrity monitoring functions: Detects changes in real-time, identifies who made the changes and when, determines authorized vs. unauthorized changes, and alert if a change takes an asset out of compliance.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for developing, documenting, and maintaining under configuration control, a current baseline configuration of the application and database.</td>
    </tr>

(a) Reviews proposed configuration-controlled changes to the information system and approves or disapproves such changes with explicit consideration for security impact analyses;

(b) Documents configuration change decisions associated with the information system;

(c) Implements approved configuration-controlled changes to the information system;

(d) Retains records of configuration-controlled changes to the information system for [Assignment: organization-defined time period];

        <th>CM-4 What is the solution and how is it implemented?</th>
        <th></th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td rowspan="2">Implemented<br/><br/>Shared (Service Provider and Customer Responsibility)<br/><br/>**VGC:** To start the process, the VGC System Administrator, Security Engineer, Domain Administrator, or Network Administrator or VGC Customer fills out a change request ticket in ServiceNow and a Security Impact Analysis (SIA) form (available for 3PAO testing). The SIA documents the business requirements for the change, a description of the change, potential security issues, change type, and device impact, and results. Prior to applying the change in the staging zone and testing it, the Security Engineers research the risks associated with implementing the change and analyze the security impact to determine if the change will negatively impact the information system, by reviewing documentation known as “Errata,” which provides prior testing results from the vendor in various environments. The VGC Security Engineers evaluate whether the proposed change affects overall system confidentiality, integrity, availability, performance, and if it opens additional ports. In some instances, FTGS Security Engineers run vulnerability scans to further verify and validate the security impact to the VGC environment.<br/><br/>Before a planned significant change takes place, the VGC Security Analyst must perform a Security Impact Analysis to determine if the change will adversely affect the security of the system. The Security Impact Analysis is a standard part of a VGC’s change control process as described in the VGC Configuration Management Plan. Any type of change is tested in the Staging Zone and the results of testing are documented in the SIA. The SIA is attached to the work order/change request form template in the Change Management module of ServiceNow.<br/><br/>The VGC Program Manager must notify the FedRAMP Program Management Office (PMO) and JAB Reviewers of any planned significant changes. The notification of the planned significant change must take place prior to the implementation of the significant change. The FTGS Security Analyst downloads the latest version of the Significant Change Form from the FedRAMP Marketplace at www.fedramp.gov. The Significant Change Form and Security Impact Analysis Form must be filled out and returned to the PMO and JAB Reviewers. The planned change will be reviewed and either be approved or rejected by the FedRAMP JAB Reviewers. All plans for significant changes should include rationale for making the change, and plans for testing the change prior to moving it to the production system.<br/><br/>If any anticipated change either adds residual risk, changes a leveraging agency’s security posture, or creates other risk exposure that the FedRAMP JAB Reviewers deems unacceptable, the Provisional Authorization could be revoked if the change is made without prior approval. VGC follows best practices by making planned changes in a controlled manner so that the security posture of the system is not weakened.<br/><br/>**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for analyzing changes to the information system to determine potential security impacts prior to change implementation.</td>
        <td></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

## CM-6 Configuration Settings (L) (M) (H)

The organization:

(a) Establishes and documents configuration settings for information technology products employed within the information system using [*FedRAMP Assignment: see CM-6(a) Additional FedRAMP Requirements and Guidance*] that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements;

> **CM-6(a) Additional FedRAMP Requirements and Guidance:**
>
> **Requirement 1:** The service provider shall use the Center for Internet Security guidelines (Level 1) to establish configuration settings or establishes its own configuration settings if USGCB is not available. If no recognized USGCB is available for the technology in use, the CSP should create their own baseline and include a justification statement as to how they came up with the baseline configuration settings.
>
> **Requirement 2:** The service provider shall ensure that checklists for configuration settings are Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) (http://scap.nist.gov/) validated or SCAP compatible (if validated checklists are not available).

> **Guidance:** Information on the USGCB checklists can be found at:
> http://usgcb.nist.gov/usgcb_faq.html#usgcbfaq_usgcbfdcc.

(d) Implements the configuration settings;
(e) Identifies, documents, and approves any deviations from established configuration settings for [Assignment: organization-defined information system components] based on [Assignment: organization-defined operational requirements]; and
(f) Monitors and controls changes to the configuration settings in accordance with organizational policies and procedures.

        <td rowspan="11">Implemented<br/><br/>Shared (Service Provider and Customer Responsibility)<br/><br/>VGC: VGC uses DISA STIG, CIS benchmarks, Nessus, and Tripwire to centrally manage, apply, and verify configuration settings for Windows and Linux servers, routers, firewalls and switches.<br/><br/>VMware uses VMware Compliance Checker tool along with VMware Nessus audit files to centrally manage, apply and verify configuration settings.<br/><br/>Trend Micro Deep Security centrally manages, applies and verifies configuration settings for antivirus on Windows and Linux servers.<br/><br/>The Group Policy Management Console is used to centrally manage, apply, and verify Windows OS configuration settings. Once the VGC Domain Administrator creates the policies, Group policy automatically enforces them by pushing them out to all Windows servers by automatically running the ‘gpupdate /force’ command.<br/><br/>Trend Micro HIDS is used to centrally manage, apply, and verify Windows OS configuration settings. The Trend Micro Manager communicates with the Trend Micro agents installed on each Windows and Linux servers and alerts via email anytime there is a configuration settings change.<br/><br/>BigFix centrally manages OS and networking appliance patches, firmware updates, and Windows security updates.<br/><br/>Tripwire is used to centrally manage, apply, and verify configuration settings via its file integrity monitoring capability. VGC Security Engineer establishes baseline configuration policies. In addition, the VGC Security Engineer configures the Tripwire console to send daily email notifications to FTGS Operations and FTGS Security teams whenever there is a change in a monitored configuration setting.<br/><br/>IL4 Implementation: Same as VGC implementation.<br/><br/>Customer Responsibility: The VGC Customer is responsible for employing automated mechanisms to centrally manage, apply, and verify configuration settings for the application and database.</td>

guidelines (Level 1) to establish list of prohibited or restricted functions, ports, protocols, and/or services or establishes its own list of prohibited or restricted functions, ports, protocols, and/or services if USGCB is not available. For Windows Server 2012 and Linux Servers, the VGC system administrator has to manually enable ports, protocols, and services explicitly by direction of an approved change request. Once the system administrator receives the request from the VGC Customer or internally, he/she opens a ticket in ServiceNow and conducts a SIA to ensure the change won’t negatively affect the VGC environment. The request and SIA are attached to the work order in ServiceNow. The change is tested in the staging/test zone prior to going to production. If there are no negative effects, the change is deployed to production. If there are negative effects, the change isn’t made and the reason is documented on the ServiceNow work order. The VGC System Administrator sends a copy of the work order with the reason for not making the change via email to the VGC Customer. The list of prohibited or restricted functions, ports, protocols, and/or services is approved and accepted by the JAB.<br/>**IL4 Implementation:** DoD-affiliated agency customer will work with FTGS to establish a list of prohibited or restricted functions, ports, protocols, and/or services or establishes its own list of prohibited or restricted functions, ports, protocols, and/or services based on guidance from IAW DoDI 8551.01.<br/>**Customer Responsibility:** The VGC Customer is responsible for documenting in their SSP how the database and application prohibits or restricts the use of the following functions, ports, protocols, and/or services.</td>
